content.text: {"answer":"The provided papers do not directly address “finding the best evidence subgraphs from a hidden knowledge graph without needing to train the system.” None of the results describe extracting evidence subgraphs from a hidden knowledge graph or an approach that avoids training for that task.\n\nWhat the supplied papers do cover is primarily stylistic analysis, authorship verification, and how language-model rewriting/personalization affects textual style (for example, voice and stylistic drift under LLM rewriting [1], authorship verification under distribution shifts [2], post-editing and style similarity [3], drift in scientific prose [4], and benchmarks/diagnostics for personalization [9,10]). Some also relate authorship signals to graph-based relationships between authors (academic genealogy) using embeddings [6], but this is not evidence-subgraph discovery from a hidden knowledge graph, and it does not match the “without needing to train” requirement based on the abstracts given.","grounded":false}
